answer:
FINAL HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded):

"Urban land use promoted UNINTENTIONAL (accidental) invasion by non-native ANNUAL FORBS. The association is strongest for the most recent urbanization (2009) measured at the intermediate 500 m buffer, and it is concentrated in urbanized habitats — above all the Urban habitat, and in the urban fringes of coastal, riparian and wetland habitats. In this scenario, plots with more urban cover around them host more unintentionally introduced annual-forb invaders (e.g., Erigeron sumatrensis, Amaranthus retroflexus, Symphyotrichum squamatum), which are also the most successful invaders in the region. By contrast, gardening-origin species show a weaker, mainly 1993-era association with urban cover, and agriculture/forestry species show no association with urban land use."

SCENARIO SPECIFICATION: pathway = Unintentional; growth form = Annual forbs (60% of unintentional species); buffer = 500 m; year = 2009; habitat = Urban (and urban-affected Coastal/Riparian/Wetlands); landscape-change class = not a driver (current urban state matters more than 1956–2009 change).

KEY EFFECT SIZES
- Unadjusted: urban.2009.500m vs log1p(n.unint): Pearson r = 0.462, Spearman rho = 0.497 — the strongest of all 27 urban×pathway pairs (n.gard max r = 0.310/rho 0.395; n.agfo ≤ 0.058).
- Negative-binomial GLM (adjusted for same-buffer/year cropland, elevation, log distance to road/stream): n.unint positive for ALL 9 urban variables (p ≤ 0.015); rate ratio per unit urban fraction 2.8–5.3; maximum at 500 m/2009: coef = 1.676 (SE 0.355), RR ≈ 5.3, p < 0.0001. n.gard significant only at 50 m/1993 (RR 2.29, p = 0.010) and 500 m/1993 (RR 2.44, p = 0.042). n.agfo: all null.
- Dose–response: mean n.unint rises monotonically across urban.2009.500m quartiles: 0.106 → 0.408 → 1.240; model-predicted count at q90 (46% urban) is ~2.1× that at the median (2% urban).
- Habitat: Urban habitat (mean 2009 urban% at 500 m = 56.6) mean n.unint = 1.60 vs 0.33 in all other habitats (Mann–Whitney p ≈ 1e-26); n.gard 0.69 vs 0.22 (p ≈ 4e-10); n.agfo no difference. Within non-urban habitats, 2009 urban% at 500 m correlates with n.unint in Coastal rho = 0.70, Riparian 0.53, Wetlands 0.44, Meadows 0.38; excluding the Urban habitat, the 500 m/2009 urban effect on n.unint remains positive (coef 1.19, p = 0.060).
- Species-level cross-reference: mean invaded plots per species: Unintentional 9.6 > Gardening 3.9 > AgriForest 2.3; Unintentional × Annual fg = 12.6 (n = 18) is the top cell; 7 of the 10 most successful species are unintentional annual forbs (Erigeron sumatrensis 53 plots, Amaranthus retroflexus 35, Symphyotrichum squamatum 34, Erigeron canadensis 29, Xanthium spp. 15/13).
- Landscape-change sensitivity: progressive/regressive 1956–2009 and 1993–2009 fractions show no robust association with any pathway (single borderline term, progressive.1993.2009.50m × n.unint, p = 0.032, sign inconsistent with rank correlations) — the signal follows current urban state, not the magnitude of change.

CAVEATS
1. Correlational: adding habitat dummies attenuates the urban coefficient to non-significance, indicating part of the association is mediated by the Urban habitat itself — which is why the hypothesis names the habitat as part of the scenario rather than claiming a context-free effect.
2. Zero-inflated counts; NegativeBinomial fitted with default dispersion (alpha = 1) in this statsmodels version.
3. 27 urban×pathway comparisons; the Unintentional signal is consistent across all 9 urban variables and both correlation and regression, supporting robustness, but no formal FDR was applied.
4. n.agfo is underpowered (pathway present in only 21 plots).
5. Growth form is known at species level (invasion_success_pathways.csv), not per plot, so the annual-forb refinement rests on the species-level composition and success of the Unintentional pathway.
6. Urban/cropland stored as fractions (0–1); reported as percentages above. 4 species flagged duplicated=TRUE were retained.

payload.hypothesis: Urban land use promoted unintentional (accidental) invasion by non-native annual forbs: the urban–invasion association is strongest for 2009 urban cover at the 500 m buffer in urbanized habitats (Urban habitat, and urban fringes of coastal, riparian and wetland habitats), where plots with more surrounding urban land host more unintentionally introduced annual-forb invaders — the same group (e.g., Erigeron sumatrensis, Amaranthus retroflexus, Symphyotrichum squamatum) that is the most successful in the region. Gardening-origin species show a weaker, mainly 1993-era association; agriculture/forestry species show none.
payload.workflow: 1) Profiled all four files (632 plots x 37 vars; 81 species; 12-cell temporal table; Newick tree). 2) Descriptive: Pearson/Spearman of 9 urban variables (3 buffers x 3 years) vs 3 pathway counts; mean urban% by pathway presence and by habitat; Mann-Whitney Urban vs other habitats. 3) Negative-binomial GLMs per pathway for all 9 buffer-year combinations, with and without habitat dummies, plus binomial presence/absence models. 4) Landscape-change sensitivity using progressive/regressive 1956-2009 and 1993-2009 fractions (continuous and dichotomized). 5) Species-level cross-reference of pathway x growth-form invasion success. 6) Selected the scenario with the strongest, most consistent positive urban association and composed the natural-language hypothesis.
